findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper onSuccess is just the optional onChanged callback, which may be undefined, so after a successful deletion the list keeps its stale cacheUpdatedAt and continues to show 'Delete cached data' with the old timestamp until a manual refetch.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering expiresAt >= now. Cached availability is only served when expiresAt is in the future (see getCachedAvailability), so an expired, unusable cache still produces a cacheUpdatedAt, causing the UI to display a cache status and offer deletion for cache that is effectively absent.

findings.title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a tRPC error
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the user the handler throws `new Error('Credential not found or access denied')`. tRPC will surface this as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error, so clients and monitoring cannot distinguish an access/lookup problem from a server failure, and the mutation's error handling behaves accordingly.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US
findings.body: The 'last updated' timestamp uses a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) regardless of the user's configured locale from useLocale. Non-English users will see US date/time ordering in an otherwise localized UI.

findings.title: Webhook helper script only works on macOS and masks failures
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS sed syntax; on GNU/Linux sed treats '' as a filename and fails, so the .env update does not work for Linux developers. Additionally, cleanup() always exits 0 and is invoked on failure paths (e.g. when no tunnel URL was extracted), so callers/CI cannot detect that the script failed.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
findings.body: The script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies. Every run may download an unpinned package from the registry, making the local cron workflow non-reproducible, slower, and broken offline; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the declared runner kept.
